judgements.reason: Both are self-contained Tau Ceti roadmaps whose spines have landed, but InductionRestriction's remainder stacks higher: integral Brauer induction, then Brauer's characterization of characters, then the cyclotomic splitting field over Schur indices and field-of-definition descent (no schurIndex anywhere), plus twisted group algebras and group central extensions feeding the Clifford obstruction. GrothendieckEulerForms' remainder - Cartan matrix in bases and unimodularity, sesquilinear chi_q on LaurentK0, bounded-complex comparisons, linear resolutions - is mostly one step off already-built machinery such as TauCeti.cartanMap and TauCeti.LaurentK0.T_smul.

ColemanPowerSeries has nothing of its own in the baseline (no Coleman declaration at all) and must first import the Iwasawa algebra Z_p[[G]], Weierstrass/specialisation theory and the Kubota-Leopoldt p-adic L-function from PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras and DirichletPadicLFunctions, then build the norm operator, the Coleman map and the fundamental exact sequence. InductionRestriction already has Mathlib's two adjunctions plus Tau Ceti's Mackey decomposition, Clifford theorem, Artin induction and Schur multiplier, and imports nothing.

ComputationalNumberTheory's closure is four times larger (83 upstream stages across 18 roadmaps against 20 across 7): CN.1 imports the Weil and Deligne bounds through FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums FF.2, CN.3 imports modular curves with algebraic Hecke correspondences and SchemeAndStackFoundations, CN.4 the Hecke/Artin L-function interface - on top of Pratt/Miller-Rabin/LLL/Round 2/Schoof and interval arithmetic, none of which exists. ColemanPowerSeries needs one narrower chain: Iwasawa algebras and Kubota-Leopoldt, then the Coleman operator and the U_infty exact sequences.

Both import the exponential-sum/Weil-bound chain through FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums FF.2 and share the ClassicalArithmeticCompletion/AnalyticNumberTheory base, but ComputationalNumberTheory adds modular curves as schemes with Hecke correspondences and differentials, SchemeAndStackFoundations and the whole Hecke/Dedekind/Artin L-function interface through AN.4, where ProbabilisticAndMetric only adds geometry of numbers and homogeneous dynamics (GN.4).
